statement: You receive a non-negative integer n. Decide whether it is odd by reading its lowest bit: n AND 1 is 1 exactly for odd numbers. Print the word odd or the word even. No division and no remainder operator are needed - the last binary digit already is the parity.
constraints: The input is a single integer on one line.

example.why: 7 is 111 in binary; its lowest bit is 1, which is the definition of odd.

hint: Mask with 1 and branch on the result; the rest of the number is irrelevant.
mistake: Checking the highest bit or the decimal last digit - parity lives in binary position zero only.
